What We Do

Full-Service Medical Toxicology Revenue Cycle Management

Toxicology billing requires precise distinction between presumptive (80305 to 80307) and definitive (80320 to 80377) drug testing codes, payer frequency limit tracking, medical review officer service billing, and LCD compliance. PMEX manages every element so your toxicology revenue is captured accurately on every specimen.

Presumptive Drug Testing

80305, 80306, and 80307 coded by testing methodology for presumptive screens.

Definitive Drug Testing

80320 to 80377 drug class codes billed per the definitive analytes identified.

Frequency Limit Tracking

Payer-specific drug test frequency limits tracked per patient to avoid automatic denials.

LCD Compliance

Local coverage determination requirements confirmed per test per payer before billing.

MRO Billing

Medical review officer review and interpretation codes billed per the MRO workflow.

Prior Authorization

High-complexity definitive panels authorized before specimen processing on qualifying payers.

Common Medical Toxicology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Definitive drug testing billed with presumptive code (80307), losing the higher definitive rate.

PMEX applies 80320 to 80377 definitive drug class codes when definitive quantitative testing is performed and documented.

Definitive panel billed for more drug classes than the lab report documents as tested.

PMEX counts the analytes from the lab report and bills only the drug class codes that correspond to tests actually performed.

Drug testing submitted at a frequency exceeding the payer limit, generating automatic denial.

PMEX tracks drug test frequency per patient per payer and bills within the allowed testing frequency for each plan.

LCD covered diagnosis not on the claim, triggering medical necessity denial.

PMEX confirms the ordering diagnosis is on the LCD covered diagnosis list before billing every drug test.

MRO interpretation service not billed alongside the toxicology panel.

PMEX identifies MRO review encounters and submits the correct interpretation code alongside the drug testing codes.

Specimen validity testing billed incorrectly or not billed when performed.

PMEX confirms specimen validity testing from the lab report and submits the correct code when validity testing is documented.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Medical Toxicology Billing

Toxicology labs lose 20 to 35 percent of revenue to code methodology errors, frequency violations, and LCD diagnosis gaps.

PATTERN 01

Definitive Testing Billed Under Presumptive Code

Definitive quantitative mass spectrometry performed for 14 drug classes. 80307 (presumptive highest complexity, $90) submitted instead of individual definitive drug class codes (80320 to 80377). Definitive codes reimburse at $25 to $75 per drug class. Total definitive revenue: $420. Revenue captured under presumptive code: $90. $330 per panel lost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies the correct definitive drug class codes (80320 to 80377) when definitive quantitative testing is performed, billing one code per drug class tested as confirmed from the laboratory report.

PATTERN 02

Frequency Limit Exceeded, Claim Denied Automatically

Commercial payer allows definitive drug testing once per 30 days per patient. Second panel ordered 18 days after the first. Claim submitted. Denied automatically at adjudication, frequency not met. Revenue lost with no appeal pathway.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks the last billed date for drug testing per patient per payer and confirms the allowed frequency window is open before submitting each panel. Tests ordered outside the allowed frequency are flagged before billing.

PATTERN 03

Drug Test Denied, Diagnosis Not on LCD Covered List

Definitive drug panel billed for a patient on chronic opioid therapy. Ordering diagnosis: low back pain (M54.51). Medicare LCD for definitive drug testing requires a specific diagnosis that indicates monitoring for substance use or chronic pain management with prescribed controlled substances. Generic back pain code not sufficient.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms the ordering diagnosis against the applicable LCD covered diagnosis list before submitting every definitive drug test. When the ordering diagnosis needs to be more specific, PMEX flags the order before billing.

Questions

Toxicology Billing Questions Answered

Presumptive testing (80305 to 80307) identifies the presence or absence of a drug class. Definitive testing (80320 to 80377) identifies and quantifies specific drugs and metabolites. The codes are mutually exclusive for the same specimen and the same drug class.

One code per drug class is billed per the specific analytes tested from the laboratory report. We count the drug classes from the lab report and apply the correct 80320 to 80377 code for each class tested.

Frequency limits vary by payer. Medicare and many commercial payers limit definitive drug testing to once per month or once per 30 days for chronic pain patients. We track frequency limits per patient per payer.

Medical review officer review and interpretation is separately billable when the MRO reviews and interprets a drug test result. We bill the correct MRO code alongside the drug testing codes when MRO review is documented.

Yes. Some commercial payers require prior authorization for definitive drug testing panels above a certain complexity level. We manage authorization before specimen processing on qualifying payers.

Within 30 days, with drug class code libraries verified and frequency tracking active from day one.
